world.bio: I'm Karim Haddad, born in Aleppo, now in Berlin. My father and grandfather were luthiers; I grew up in the workshop in the old souq, sanding rib after rib. After 2015 I rebuilt a small workshop in a courtyard in Wedding. I make and repair ouds for players across Europe: Arabic ouds, Turkish ouds, a few Persian barbats. Winter is my slow season.
skills_assets: Makes and repairs ouds in a Wedding courtyard workshop; winter is his slow season
Three generations of oud-making knowledge: bent ribs, bowl-back construction, soundboard bracing
Workshop with a steam bender, rib moulds, hand planes, and a spray booth I rarely use
A client list of about 150 players across Germany, the Netherlands, France
Fluent Arabic, German (B2, still improving), good English, some French

projects.name: Commission: Turkish oud for a Rotterdam player
projects.text: A twelve-string oud in the Istanbul style, walnut ribs, spruce top, ebony bridge. The rosette is hand-cut. I'm on week five; the soundboard bracing is the hardest part. He wants it by December.

projects.name: Citizenship application
projects.text: Gathering documents for German naturalisation: language certificate, employment records, the integration course certificate. The appointment at the Bezirksamt is on the 14th of October.

notes.text: Morning in the workshop. Planed the soundboard of the Rotterdam oud until it sang when tapped. My father used to say a good board talks back. Had tea with the neighbour who fixes bicycles. We don't share much language but we share the courtyard.

Helped my nephew Omar with his school paperwork. The Anmeldung for the Gymnasium needs a form that nobody can explain. We spent two hours at the Bürgeramt. He said 'Uncle, do Germans like forms?' I said it's their folk art.
Sunday at the café, backgammon with Abu Walid. He beat me three times in a row; I blamed the dice. He said nobody has lost to the dice, only to the player.

A client from Hamburg sent me his oud with a cracked top. Looks like humidity damage. I can repair that: open the seam, relevel, glue with hide glue. He asked if I could also repaint it with lacquer. I said no. I only work on bent-rib lute bodies with gut and nylon strings; I turn down lacquer work and anything strung with silk. I'm not that kind of workshop.

Winter is coming and the workshop is cold. The little stove struggles. Last January my glue froze solid. I need to insulate the north wall before the real cold comes, a weekend job and about 400 euros.

Naturalisation test practice questions. 'Which of these is a German state?' 'What is the Grundgesetz?' I answered everything correctly except the question about the number of Bundesländer. Sixteen. I wrote it on my hand.
Missed Aleppo today. A video on the phone: the souq roof, a seller of olive soap. My cousin sent it. I watched it four times. My daughter asked why I was crying and I said it was the glue fumes.
Had a message from a Turkish oud player who wants to commission two instruments for a Berlin festival. I said yes to one. Winter is slow, so work is welcome, but I won't rush the soundboards.
Shopped for strings: gut from a supplier in Italy, nylon from a German maker. The price of gut has doubled. A short conversation with the supplier; he says it's the sheep.
German citizenship interview prep with a volunteer, a retired teacher named Frau Berger. She corrects my 'der, die, das' without mercy. Afterwards she gave me plum cake.

messages.text:
Client: Karim, how is the oud?
Me: The top is on, the bracing is next.
Client: December is fine. Take your time.

Omar: Uncle, can you sign this form?
Me: Which one?
Omar: The one that says you are my guardian for the school trip.
Me: Bring it tomorrow.

Client: Can you restore the oud with lacquer? I want it shiny.
Me: Sorry, I don't do lacquer. I can repair the crack and refinish with shellac only.
Client: Understood.

Abu Walid: Sunday again?
Me: Yes, but no excuses about the dice.
Abu Walid: The dice are honest.

Frau Berger: Next week we practise the interview.
Me: Thank you. I will bring dates.
Frau Berger: Bring tea too.

relations.about: Twelve years old, living with me while his parents settle papers
Retired German teacher, volunteers for language support

constraints: Only works on bent-rib lute bodies with gut and nylon strings
Turns down lacquer work and anything strung with silk
Cannot work after 8pm; neighbours complain about the planer
sensitive: Homesick for Aleppo, sometimes hard to work
Worried that German bureaucracy will refuse the citizenship application
